key_insight: Quantum-network control should choose between analytical computation, stochastic simulation, or learned surrogates for fidelity estimation depending on how much random memory and entanglement dynamics affect the path.
engineering_relevance: Accurate and low-latency fidelity prediction can improve routing, scheduling, purification, and memory-allocation decisions in future quantum networks.
method: Compare three estimation modes: compute analytically, simulate dynamics, or learn a surrogate.
Use a compute/simulate/learn framework tailored to end-to-end fidelity as a stochastic target.
Demonstrate the approach with a simulation-based proof of concept.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that analytical composition works in simple regimes, simulation is needed when memory effects drive fidelity variability, and lightweight learned surrogates approximate simulator outputs at much lower runtime cost.
watch_item: The main deployment challenge is sim-to-real transfer and generalization, since fidelity depends on stochastic, network-specific quantum effects that may be expensive to label and hard to model universally.
paper_title: Quality-of-Transmission Estimation in Quantum Networks: Compute, Simulate, or Learn?
